target_customer: Small sales teams of 1 to 200 people, especially YC startups, sending outbound email sequences
problem: Small teams sent personalized outbound sales emails manually or with single-channel tools. PersistIQ automated sequences, A/B tests and CRM sync for the whole outbound workflow.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, free tier at launch

technical_complexity.rationale: Email sequencing, tracking and CRM integrations are standard SaaS work; deliverability is the main hard part.

defensibility.rationale: Workflow and CRM integrations create modest lock-in, but many comparable sales engagement tools existed and later became crowded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Salesforce Ventures invested in 2015 rather than competing. The company was sold to Wishpond in March 2021 for about 3 million dollars in cash, shares and earn-out.

market_need_then: Outbound sales was moving to software, and the company cited hundreds of customers by July 2015, including ZenPayroll, per TechCrunch.

branding.domain_note: persistiq.com; the site now shows PersistIQ by Wishpond.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as the sales engagement platform for small teams.

rebrands.why: Acquisition by Wishpond; name kept as a sub-brand.

brand_strength.rationale: The name fit the persistence of follow-up emails and survived acquisition as a sub-brand, but no sourced evidence of community or viral brand effect.

outcome_analysis: PersistIQ grew from a YC Summer 2014 free email automation tool into a small sales engagement vendor with about 780 clients and about 1.1 million dollars in recurring revenue in 2020 at roughly 20 percent EBITDA margin. It raised a 1.7 million dollar seed in 2015 and then little more. Wishpond bought it in March 2021 for about 3 million dollars including an earn-out. It was a profitable but sub-venture-scale outcome in a crowded category.
notes: Seed confirmed by TechCrunch (opened) and by FinSMEs and Seedtable snippets. Round date is the announcement; TechCrunch says it closed months earlier. Exit amount of 3 million is the headline total made up of 1 million cash, 1 million shares and an earn-out of roughly 1 million capped at 2 million, so it is not all paid. No competitor sources dated near 2014 were found (TechCrunch 2015 names none); later comparison sites list Yesware, Tout and Mixmax but are undated. Founder education and employers not found. Funding after 2015 not found.
